metrics_note: accuracy, log loss, Brier score and ECE (10 equal-width bins on the top probability) with 95% percentile bootstrap intervals, resampling items, or whole groups where a tier's items carry one (interval_unit; groups is their number); 'selective' is accuracy and coverage when only answers whose top probability is above the threshold (strictly greater) are kept

test.note: in-distribution: the fit tier's test split

final.note: fresh held-out families, frozen before any head was scored on them: the reported result

final-flagged.note: fresh held-out families with a recorded caveat (see `caveats`): reported beside the final result, never pooled into it, judging no bar

caveats.healthfc: The evidence sentences are the fact-checkers' own summary and often state the verdict ("we could not find any meaningful scientific evidence", verdict headings such as "Not checked"), so the no-bearing label (the verdict "insufficient evidence") can often be read off the wording, the flaw that excluded PubHealth; and 740 of the 749 claims are yes/no questions, not claims.

final-seen.note: secondary evaluation: an earlier held-out tier, its families seen during development
